scope: acquisition and the installed index footprint; component-rights and offline-reader admission pending

components.name: appropedia-dense-vectors
components.basis: 22336 indexed HTML entries, the counter recorded in the checked inspection receipt content/inspections/appropedia-2026-02-html-v4.json, one vector each at the encoder's 384 dimensions and the profile schema's default float32 vector datatype. Rights exclusions and a non-canonical selection policy can only lower the count, and a float16 profile halves the width

components.name: appropedia-dense-graph
components.basis: Qdrant's published capacity formula hnsw_size = points x m x 2 x 4 bytes x 1.2 at its default m of 16 (https://qdrant.tech/documentation/capacity-planning/); the collection adapters.Qdrant.create builds keeps the graph on disk and overrides no HNSW parameter

components.name: appropedia-dense-payload
components.basis: Qdrant's published disk_size = points x avg_payload_size x 1.5, whose 1.5 covers backend storage overhead. Every point carries the same four-field record adapters.Qdrant.put builds, 394 bytes compactly encoded at this archive's widest entry index of 65155

components.name: appropedia-passage-spans
components.basis: the article-spans artifact stores each article's extracted blocks, spans and representative compressed at zlib level 6. The only measured constant, 3190 bytes per article in oracle_content.precompute, was sampled from English Wikipedia and does not transfer to this archive's entries; sampling this archive is what would quantify it. The builder publishes whatever it reaches and stops at its own --min-free-bytes floor, so an unreserved shortfall costs coverage rather than the install

components.name: dense-index-headroom
components.basis: the ~20% disk headroom the same Qdrant capacity page recommends, taken over the vector, graph and payload components it covers: the write-ahead log, snapshots and the optimizer's temporary segments. The article-spans artifact is a SQLite file outside the vector store and is deliberately not in this sum

components.name: shared-service-runtime
components.basis: indexing writes into the shared content state and the shared Qdrant store, and adds no per-pack runtime working set; the service's own bounded stores (CONTENT_SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES, CONTENT_FAILURE_LOG_MAX_BYTES) belong to the installation rather than to any one pack and are not multiplied by it

components.name: archive-second-copy
components.basis: prepare_native hardlinks the verified archive into the content state, so the original occupies its pinned artifact bytes once; a content state on another filesystem cannot hardlink and needs that many bytes again, which is a layout choice this manifest cannot see
